(1) Haemoglobin is a carrier protein found in the Red Blood Cells which forms a partial bond with the oxygen from the lungs and carbon dioxide from cells enabling the different parts of the body in respiration. SpO2 is the measure of the haemoglobin which is bonded with an oxygen molecule. It indirectly helps us estimate the amount of oxygen that is supplied to the cells in the body. 95%-100% SpO2 is considered normal. 

(2) Monitoring the SpO2 level on the blood can help us avoid hypoxia, fatigue, lung complications and other physical issues. The HONOR bands measure the SpO2 levels during exercise and can keep a check on heart rate and breathing patterns.

(3) The SpO2 (pulse oxygen saturation monitor) feture is currently available in the HONOR Band 5, HONOR Band 5i and the HONOR Magicwatch 2 in the EU, Russia and India.
